items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I was sitting on a park bench with Howard McGhee on August 30, 1973 and we’re listening to the Charlie Parker Festival eating ice cream.

ctx.x: WABC — Steven K. Nenno was his name. So the Charlie Parker Festival, this is the turning point of KCR. I started February 2, of ’70. I’m doing what I did already. But only a few people are listening. One of them is Tristano and he calls up to yell at me. But then I did the Charlie Parker Festival. Or really Irv Schenkler did the Charlie Parker Festival using my Charlie Parker chops. I’m the guy, he’s the producer. That’s a fair operation. And Tristano says, “Phil got the right idea.” And so he calls the studio…

’73 I did the Fletcher Henderson Festival. And then okay, fine. And I get this phone call and says “I am Steven K. Nenno” — this is WABC who had a radio network at the time — “I’m in charge of, you know Arbitron is one thing but we do our own radio listings. And I need to talk to you. I’d like to come to WKCR and check out your operation.” So you know I’m 22 at the time, this could be big. He’s not the police, I’m not going to get arrested, or what could he do to me? So I go yeah. So he shows up and he literally…
